segment_reference_payload.description: Segment Redshift warehouse destination output for a track event — S3 staging with COPY command via manifest

manifest.notes: Segment generates a JSON manifest listing all CSV.GZ part files for a given table and sync interval

copy_command.template: COPY {schema}.{table} FROM 's3://{bucket}/{manifest_key}' CREDENTIALS 'aws_access_key_id={key};aws_secret_access_key={secret}' MANIFEST CSV GZIP DATEFORMAT 'auto' TIMEFORMAT 'auto' TRUNCATECOLUMNS EMPTYASNULL BLANKSASNULL FILLRECORD ACCEPTANYDATE TRIMBLANKS ACCEPTINVCHARS COMPUPDATE OFF STATUPDATE OFF;

table_creation.notes: Segment uses DISTSTYLE EVEN by default; SORTKEY on received_at for time-range query optimization

identifies.notes: Trait columns are added dynamically based on incoming identify traits

users.notes: Trait columns merged from identifies table; latest trait values per user_id

rudderstack_expected_payload.description: RudderStack Redshift warehouse destination output for a track event — S3 staging with COPY command via manifest

manifest.notes: RudderStack generates a JSON manifest with entries array; each entry includes url, mandatory flag, and metadata (content_length). Manifests are uploaded to a separate S3 path under rudder-redshift-manifests/

copy_command.csv_template: COPY {schema}.{staging_table}({sorted_column_names}) FROM '{s3_manifest_location}' CSV GZIP ACCESS_KEY_ID '{temp_key}' SECRET_ACCESS_KEY '{temp_secret}' SESSION_TOKEN '{token}' REGION '{region}' DATEFORMAT 'auto' TIMEFORMAT 'auto' MANIFEST TRUNCATECOLUMNS EMPTYASNULL BLANKSASNULL FILLRECORD ACCEPTANYDATE TRIMBLANKS ACCEPTINVCHARS COMPUPDATE OFF STATUPDATE OFF;
copy_command.parquet_template: COPY {schema}.{staging_table} FROM '{s3_manifest_location}' ACCESS_KEY_ID '{temp_key}' SECRET_ACCESS_KEY '{temp_secret}' SESSION_TOKEN '{token}' MANIFEST FORMAT PARQUET;
copy_command.notes: RudderStack supports both CSV GZIP and Parquet load file formats. CSV COPY includes full set of data handling options; Parquet COPY is simplified. Temporary STS credentials are obtained via GetTemporaryS3Cred(). Alternative: folder-based loading without manifest when loadByFolderPath is enabled.

table_creation.dist_key_condition: Applied only when 'id' column exists in table schema; otherwise no explicit DISTSTYLE
table_creation.create_table_template: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {schema}.{table} ({column_definitions}) DISTSTYLE KEY DISTKEY("id") SORTKEY("{sort_key_field}")
table_creation.notes: RudderStack uses DISTSTYLE KEY with DISTKEY on 'id' column when present, optimizing joins/dedup on the primary key. Sort key prefers received_at for time-range query efficiency.

identifies.notes: Trait columns added dynamically as varchar(65535) based on incoming identify events

users.dedup_strategy: FIRST_VALUE({column} IGNORE NULLS) OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY received_at DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
users.notes: Users table is built from identifies via FIRST_VALUE window function to get latest non-null trait per user_id. Uses staging table approach with UNION of existing users and new identifies.

rudder_discards.notes: Discards table stores rows that failed schema validation or type conversion

merge_flow: 1. Create staging table (LIKE source table INCLUDING DEFAULTS)
2. COPY data from S3 into staging table via manifest
3. DELETE from main table WHERE primary_key matches staging table
4. INSERT into main table from staging with ROW_NUMBER() dedup (PARTITION BY partition_key ORDER BY received_at DESC)

dedup_window.notes: When enabled, DELETE step adds received_at > GETDATE() - INTERVAL 'N HOUR' to limit dedup scope

append_only_tables.notes: Per-destination per-table override to force append-only (no merge)

iam_role.notes: IAM role-based auth via sqlconnect-go with workspace-specific role ARN and external ID

manifest_file_format.segment: JSON manifest with entries array containing {url, mandatory} per load file
manifest_file_format.rudderstack: JSON manifest with entries array containing {url, mandatory, meta: {content_length}} per load file
manifest_file_format.parity_gap: RudderStack includes content_length metadata per manifest entry; Segment does not. Manifest upload paths differ: Segment stores alongside load files, RudderStack uses separate rudder-redshift-manifests/ prefix.
manifest_file_format.impact: Low — both produce valid Redshift MANIFEST-compatible JSON; metadata field is informational

copy_options.segment: COPY with CREDENTIALS string, CSV GZIP, DATEFORMAT/TIMEFORMAT auto, TRUNCATECOLUMNS, EMPTYASNULL, BLANKSASNULL, FILLRECORD, ACCEPTANYDATE, TRIMBLANKS, ACCEPTINVCHARS, COMPUPDATE OFF, STATUPDATE OFF, MANIFEST
copy_options.rudderstack: COPY with ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/SESSION_TOKEN (STS), CSV GZIP or FORMAT PARQUET, REGION, same data handling options as Segment for CSV; simplified options for Parquet
parity_gaps: Auth: Segment uses CREDENTIALS string; RudderStack uses separate ACCESS_KEY_ID + SECRET_ACCESS_KEY + SESSION_TOKEN parameters (STS temporary credentials)
Format: RudderStack supports both CSV GZIP and Parquet; Segment uses CSV GZIP
Region: RudderStack explicitly includes REGION clause; Segment may omit it
Column list: RudderStack specifies explicit column list in COPY for CSV; Segment may omit column list
copy_options.impact: Medium — auth mechanism differs but both authenticate successfully; Parquet support is RudderStack-unique advantage

auth_method.segment: AWS access key credentials embedded in CREDENTIALS string
auth_method.rudderstack: Temporary STS credentials (ACCESS_KEY_ID + SECRET_ACCESS_KEY + SESSION_TOKEN) or IAM role-based authentication via sqlconnect-go with workspace-specific role ARN
auth_method.parity_gap: RudderStack supports two auth methods (password and IAM role) vs Segment's single access-key method. IAM role auth with serverless Redshift support is RudderStack-unique.
auth_method.impact: Low — functionally equivalent; RudderStack offers more auth flexibility

sort_key_strategy.segment: SORTKEY(received_at) — received_at as default sort key for all tables
sort_key_strategy.rudderstack: SORTKEY({field}) with priority: received_at > uuid_ts > id — dynamically selected based on available columns in table schema
sort_key_strategy.parity_gap: RudderStack has dynamic sort key selection with fallback chain; Segment uses static received_at. Both typically resolve to received_at for standard event tables.
sort_key_strategy.impact: Low — in practice both use received_at for standard tables; RudderStack handles edge cases where received_at is absent

dist_key_strategy.segment: DISTSTYLE EVEN — distributes data evenly across nodes regardless of key values
dist_key_strategy.rudderstack: DISTSTYLE KEY DISTKEY("id") — distributes data by id column when present, enabling co-located joins; no explicit DISTSTYLE when id column is absent
dist_key_strategy.parity_gap: Fundamental distribution strategy difference: Segment uses EVEN (optimal for scan-heavy workloads), RudderStack uses KEY on id (optimal for join-heavy dedup/merge workloads). This affects query performance characteristics.
dist_key_strategy.impact: High — affects query performance for merge/dedup operations. RudderStack's KEY distribution co-locates rows with same id on same node, optimizing the DELETE+INSERT merge pattern. Segment's EVEN distribution spreads data uniformly.

string_column_length.parity_gap: RudderStack uses VARCHAR(65535) while Segment uses VARCHAR(512). RudderStack defines rudderStringLength=512 constant but maps string type to varchar(65535).
string_column_length.impact: Low — both store the same data; RudderStack's wider columns avoid truncation for long values but may use more disk space

boolean_encoding.parity_gap: RudderStack applies run-length encoding to boolean columns for compression optimization
boolean_encoding.impact: None — storage optimization only; query behavior identical

json_type.parity_gap: RudderStack uses Redshift's native SUPER type for JSON data; Segment stores JSON as VARCHAR string
json_type.impact: Medium — SUPER type enables native JSON querying with PartiQL; VARCHAR requires JSON parsing functions

dedup_merge_strategy.segment: Upsert via staging table with dedup on primary key
dedup_merge_strategy.rudderstack: Configurable merge/append: staging table COPY, DELETE matching primary keys, INSERT with ROW_NUMBER() dedup partitioned by partition_key ordered by received_at DESC. Supports append-only mode, dedup window, per-destination skip, per-table append-only overrides.
dedup_merge_strategy.parity_gap: RudderStack offers significantly more granular dedup control (per-destination, per-table, time-windowed). Users table has special FIRST_VALUE-based trait dedup.
dedup_merge_strategy.impact: Low-Medium — both achieve data deduplication; RudderStack provides more operational flexibility

table_name_limit.parity_gap: RudderStack explicitly enforces 127-character table name limit for staging table name generation
table_name_limit.impact: None — Redshift enforces this limit regardless

staging_table_naming.rudderstack: warehouseutils.StagingTableName(provider, tableName, tableNameLimit) — generates prefixed staging table names with RS provider tag
staging_table_naming.parity_gap: Different staging table naming conventions; staging tables are transient and dropped after loading

connection_management.rudderstack: PostgreSQL connection with configurable timeout, slow query threshold (default 5 min), query_group set to 'RudderStack', secret redaction in logs, sqlmiddleware wrapper with stats/logging/KV tagging
connection_management.parity_gap: RudderStack has more sophisticated connection management with observability built in

high_parity_areas: S3 staging approach (both use S3 → COPY with manifest)
COPY command core options (DATEFORMAT, TIMEFORMAT, TRUNCATECOLUMNS, etc.)
Table structure (tracks, identifies, users, pages, screens, groups, aliases)
parity_gaps: DISTSTYLE: EVEN (Segment) vs KEY on id (RudderStack) — impacts query performance
Auth: CREDENTIALS string (Segment) vs STS temp credentials + IAM role option (RudderStack)
JSON type: VARCHAR (Segment) vs SUPER (RudderStack) — impacts JSON querying
File format: CSV only (Segment) vs CSV + Parquet (RudderStack)
Manifest metadata: No content_length (Segment) vs content_length included (RudderStack)
rudderstack_unique_features: Parquet file format support for COPY loading
IAM role-based authentication with serverless Redshift support
SUPER type for native JSON/semi-structured data
DISTSTYLE KEY optimization for merge-heavy workloads
SSH tunnel support for password-based connections
Slow query threshold monitoring and secret redaction in logs

notes: Redshift is a shared warehouse destination present in both RudderStack and Segment. Both platforms use the same fundamental approach: stage data files to S3, then use Redshift's COPY command with a JSON manifest to bulk load data. Key architectural differences are in distribution strategy (EVEN vs KEY), authentication (access keys vs STS/IAM), and data type mapping (VARCHAR vs SUPER for JSON). RudderStack's implementation in warehouse/integrations/redshift/redshift.go provides significantly more operational flexibility with configurable merge/append modes, dedup windows, and per-destination overrides. The payload parity gaps are primarily in table DDL (sort/dist key strategies, column widths) rather than in the event data itself. Source: warehouse/integrations/redshift/redshift.go, docs/gap-report/destination-catalog-parity.md line 385.
